summary: Signed a 4-year, $64M extension in May ($32M guaranteed) and enters 2026 as the clear centerpiece of Miami's offense after a Pro Bowl 2025 season; missed OTAs/minicamp recovering from offseason shoulder surgery but was a full go with no restrictions once training camp opened. Coaching staff has said the offense will run through him.

Agreed to a 2-year, $44M extension ($39M guaranteed) with the Colts in early August 2026, signed through 2028 rather than hitting free agency next offseason. Unlike several other top backs (Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs) he did not hold in to get it. Remains Indianapolis's clear workhorse starter.

Taking the clear majority of first-team reps through the first several practices of Bengals camp over free-agent signee Zack Moss, and has been one of the most encouraging stories of camp with 191 all-purpose preseason yards plus a long TD run. Primed for his largest workload yet in Zac Taylor's offense.
Entrenched as the Rams' starter through camp with Blake Corum as clear backup and Jarquez Hunter/Ronnie Rivers competing for a depth spot; no notable change to his role from 2025.

Held in during part of camp awaiting a new contract before agreeing to a 4-year, $48M extension ($30M guaranteed) that runs through 2029. Situation is fully resolved; no lingering distraction expected into the season.

Had a brief knee scare during an OTA 11-on-11 drill in May (knocked knees with a teammate) but walked off under his own power and returned to practice minutes later. No lasting issue; entered training camp fully healthy in his 11th season.

Adjusting to a new offensive scheme/playcaller in Philadelphia after last season's staff turnover; has looked explosive and broken long runs in camp, with his workload being deliberately managed in the preseason to have him at full strength for the September 13 opener at Washington.

Fully recovered from the shoulder surgery that cost him 7 games and significant snaps in 2025 (he also dealt with a foot injury the same stretch); HC Todd Bowles called him a "full-go" for training camp with no ramp-up period needed.

Left a mid-August practice early with a groin injury; the Jets are tracking him for Week 1 vs. Tennessee and aren't showing much concern. New OC Frank Reich has reinforced a commitment to featuring Hall and Garrett Wilson more prominently in 2026's offense.

Expected to open the season as Dallas's RB1, running decisively and looking comfortable in Brian Schottenheimer's offense through the first practices of camp — but rookie Jaydon Blue (see separate note) is pushing hard for touches.

Flashing big-play burst throughout Cowboys camp, including a reported 40-50 yard outside-zone run that multiple reporters said would have stood up live, and is genuinely complicating Javonte Williams' hold on the lead role rather than settling in as a clear-cut backup.

Denver's unofficial depth chart lists J.K. Dobbins (now healthy) ahead of Harvey, but Harvey's pass-catching (356 receiving yards as a rookie vs. Dobbins' 37) gives him a real receiving-down role behind the presumed early-down starter.
Now healthy after the Lisfranc foot injury that limited him late in 2025, and has been a full participant in camp as Denver's listed RB1 ahead of RJ Harvey.

Signed a 4-year, ~$48M deal with New Orleans in free agency and enters 2026 as the team's clear RB1 coming off a career-best 13-touchdown season in Jacksonville. Coach Kellen Moore has said he'll find ways to use both Etienne and Alvin Kamara, but Etienne is described as the current top back.

Restructured his contract to stay in New Orleans through 2026 rather than being cap-cut, but now shares the backfield with newly-signed Travis Etienne (see separate note) at age 31 — a real timeshare rather than the workhorse role he's held historically.

Fully cleared and a full-go for training camp, seven months after surgery for a fractured fibula and dislocated ankle suffered in Week 16, 2025. Coming off a strong rookie season (827 rush yards, 7 TD in fewer than 16 games) and projects as Cleveland's top running back for 2026.

New England is planning a genuine 50/50 backfield split with Rhamondre Stevenson in 2026, with Henderson leaning toward passing-down/big-play work after leading the team in touches, yards, and TDs as a rookie. Not the clear-cut lead-back role his rookie usage alone would suggest.

Splitting New England's backfield roughly 50/50 with TreVeyon Henderson in 2026, expected to handle early-down and short-yardage work after closing 2025 strong (5.7 YPC over his final 8 games including playoffs).

Houston has deployed Marks and newly-acquired David Montgomery (see separate note) in near-even workloads throughout camp, a true committee rather than a clear starter/backup, despite Marks leading the team in rushing as a rookie in 2025.

Traded from Detroit to Houston in March 2026 (for a 2026 4th, a 2027 7th, and a lineman); last season's Lions committee context (with Jahmyr Gibbs) no longer applies. Now in a near-even camp committee with 2nd-year back Woody Marks rather than a clear role.

Signed a 1-year, $2M deal with Washington in March after finishing as Tampa Bay's RB2 behind Bucky Irving. Enters a committee with 2nd-year back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, expected to take the pass-catching role given his dual-threat profile.

Coming off a strong 7th-round-rookie finish in 2025 (805 rush yards, 8 TD on 175 carries), the Commanders view him as the vision/burst piece of a committee with newly-signed Rachaad White, who takes more of the receiving work.

Signed with Pittsburgh in free agency and is splitting first-team reps in camp with incumbent Jaylen Warren rather than clearly winning the job outright, despite rushing for 1,076 yards in Carolina last season. Reunites with new Steelers HC Mike McCarthy, his former Cowboys coach.

Splitting first-team reps with free-agent addition Rico Dowdle rather than being displaced outright; OC Brian Angelichio has said both backs will be a big part of the offense. A genuine committee, not a clean loss of role.

Tore his ACL in January 2026 and had surgery the following month; placed on the PUP list July 22, which requires missing at least the first 4 games of the season. Rookie Jadarian Price (see separate note) is expected to lead the backfield early instead.

Seattle's No. 32 overall 2026 draft pick has been a standout early in camp and is positioned to lead the backfield (likely alongside Emanuel Wilson) while Zach Charbonnet recovers from a torn ACL; Seattle also lost 2025 starter Kenneth Walker III to Kansas City in free agency, so the incumbent context from last season is gone entirely.
Named one of the Titans' two "bell cows" (with Tyjae Spears) by HC Robert Saleh and remains the presumptive starter in new OC Brian Daboll's offense, entering the final year of his contract.

Positioned for a bigger role as both a runner and receiver in new OC Brian Daboll's offense alongside Tony Pollard; has struggled to stay healthy the past two seasons, so his 2025 per-game numbers may understate his real 2026 role if he stays on the field.

Real roster-bubble risk despite being the presumed RB2 behind Cam Skattebo: two costly preseason mistakes (a missed pass-pro block that led to a hit on QB Jaxson Dart, and a lost fumble at the 10-yard line) drew public criticism from HC John Harbaugh, and the Giants have since given Devin Singletary first-team preseason reps ahead of him after also signing veteran Najee Harris. Last season's role is not guaranteed to carry over.

Sideline reporters at Vikings camp have generally said Jordan Mason looks like the clear RB1 and has been "taking a leap" this camp, ahead of Jones — a real threat to the lead-back role Jones has held.

Arizona's published depth chart lists him 5th at the position — behind Tyler Allgeier, rookie Jeremiyah Love, James Conner, and Trey Benson (since waived) — with only Corey Kiner behind him. Minimal realistic path to meaningful 2026 touches barring multiple injuries ahead of him.

No longer with Kansas City — the Chiefs replaced him and Isiah Pacheco this offseason with free-agent signee Kenneth Walker III. Hunt remained an unsigned free agent as of late August 2026 and visited the Detroit Lions on August 25, with a deal reportedly being finalized. His team should not be read as Kansas City for 2026 regardless of what any pre-camp roster snapshot shows.

Re-signed on an exclusive-rights tender after leading the Chargers with 155 carries for 643 yards in 2025, but the team also added Keaton Mitchell in free agency alongside 2025 1st-rounder Omarion Hampton — a three-way backfield now rather than a clear No. 2 role.
